members.name: Rocco Ramadori
members.bio: Rocco is an Italian-Canadian student pursuing a Bachelors degree in economics and management. He has worked at the tech startup BrainboxAI, which uses artificial intelligence to reduce buildings' energy consumption and emissions. He hopes to create a business environment where environmental protections are not seen as an obstacle to economic activity but as a measure against resource erosion and humanitarian disasters, ultimately improving the economic outlook.

members.name: Andrea Seet
members.bio: Andrea is a Singapore-qualified lawyer with four years of experience in disputes and international arbitration. She also worked at the Law Society of Singapore as a Special Legal Projects Officer, where she supported strategic legal and policy initiatives through research, analysis, and implementation. Driven to bridge her commercial and legal advocacy experience with her commitment to social and environmental impact, Andrea is currently pursuing a Master's in Sustainability and Social Innovation at HEC Paris, graduating in 2026.

members.name: Ana Maria Lopes

Passionate about bridging the gap between science and policy, Ana Maria aspires to drive positive societal change by ensuring that ambitious climate and development policies are both technically sound and practically feasible.

members.name: Rafael Valente

Growing up in Brussels, he developed an early interest in the EU. Striving to contribute towards a carbon-neutral society, he aims to apply his skills to EU climate policy and help advance the Union's environmental goals.

members.name: Federica Marini
members.bio: Federica is Italian, Chinese, and Japanese and grew up in NYC before moving to Milan to pursue the Bachelor's in Economic and Social Sciences at Bocconi University. Since graduating, she has been working as a sustainability consultant, where she has become familiar with the political landscape of corporate sustainability and learned how to quantify the environmental impacts of businesses. This coming fall, she will begin the Erasmus Mundus Joint Master's in European Environmental Economics and Policy at the University of Copenhagen. She is interested in the economics of climate change, particularly of natural resources, global food supply chains, and public health. Alongside these studies, she is very passionate about intersectional environmentalism and environmental justice. She, therefore, is always advocating for nature and Indigenous science-based solutions to be at the forefront of drafting global solutions to climate change.

members.interests: Corporate sustainability, Environmental impacts quantification, Intersectional environmentalism, Environmental justice, Food supply chains

members.name: Lucas Lestido

He is most interested in the fields of socio-ecological economics, environmental anthropology and Social Sciences.

members.name: Alexander Martin
members.bio: Alexander is a South African-Italian Global Law student at Bocconi University, with experience in sustainability research, compliance, and market analysis across South Africa, Dubai, and Europe. He has contributed to supply-chain and market studies at Umicore and supported administrative and compliance functions at CM & Associates. He is interested in how legal and financial frameworks can enhance ESG performance and promote climate-resilient economic growth. Alexander has earned awards in debate and public speaking, having participated in competitions across Europe, Asia, and Africa, and has been engaged in community initiatives in Italy and South Africa. He aims to apply his global perspective and analytical skills to ESG and climate-focused roles within financial institutions and international organizations.
members.interests: ESG performance, Legal frameworks, Compliance market analysis, Climate-resilient growth

members.name: Michela Miglio
members.bio: Michela Miglio is a dedicated and ambitious student pursuing a Bachelor's degree in International Politics and Government at Bocconi University. Her main interest lies in how the defense sector is shaped by the interplay between public and private actors - from the role of antitrust and M&A in structuring markets to how corporate strategy and private capital can strengthen national defense capabilities. She has deepened this focus through both academic and professional experiences, including an internship at the Italian Ministry of Enterprises, where she contributed to projects on defense industrial policy and the application of golden power regulations. Michela also founded Praesidium, a magazine dedicated to defense and cybersecurity created in collaboration with a former Italian Army general. She has served as Head of Public Affairs at a Bocconi-based think tank on defense and geopolitics, leading a team that organized high-level events with experts and policymakers. In addition, she organizes career service initiatives within a student representative association, fostering connections between students and major firms. Driven by a strong commitment to European security and industrial cooperation, Michela is determined to contribute to a more integrated and competitive European defense ecosystem.
members.interests: Defense sector, Antitrust and M&A, Corporate strategy, Private capital, Defense industrial policy, Golden power regulations

members.name: Aleksandra Grbović Bitić
members.bio: Aleksandra Grbović Bitić is a dual-degree student in astrophysics and law in Belgrade, passionate about the intersection of science, strategy, and international governance. As one of Serbia's Young European Ambassadors (DG NEAR), Aleksandra promotes EU values and regional cooperation across the Western Balkans through youth-led initiatives and public dialogue. She is the founder of the Association for Contemporary Youth Education (USEM), a nonprofit dedicated to empowering young people through creative programs that blend arts, science, technology, and civic engagement. Her interests in space governance, dual-use infrastructure, and ethical defense technologies reflect her commitment to building a more resilient and inclusive Europe. Her previous work spans UNA Serbia, the Serbian Chamber of Commerce, and several long-term volunteering programs in which she has been deeply involved. She continues to contribute to grassroots and institutional initiatives that strengthen youth participation, democratic resilience, and evidence-based policymaking in the Western Balkans region.
members.companies: Young European Ambassadors (DG NEAR), Association for Contemporary Youth Education (USEM), UNA Serbia, Serbian Chamber of Commerce
members.interests: Space governance, Dual-use infrastructure, Ethical defense technologies, International governance, Science and strategy

members.name: Giacomo Bortolazzi
members.bio: Giacomo Bortolazzi is a master's student in International Security Studies at the University of Trento and Sant'Anna School of Advanced Studies. His main interests are focused on European defence and deterrence efforts, intelligence cycles and the study of collaborative efforts between the EU and other relevant military partners. These interests have been put in practice through participation in other authoritative think tanks such as ITSS and in several publications in blogs and magazines such as Praesidium, Scenari Internazionali, International Relations Today, or the Forum for Global Human Rights. Giacomo is pushed by a research-driven approach, a strong legal background, and aims at building a career in the defence and intelligence realms.
members.uni: University of Trento, Sant'Anna School of Advanced Studies
members.companies: ITSS, Praesidium, Scenari Internazionali, International Relations Today, Forum for Global Human Rights
members.interests: European defence, Deterrence efforts, Intelligence cycles, EU military partnerships

members.name: Marie Helene Olafsen
members.bio: Marie Helene Olafsen is a Politics and International Relations student at the London School of Economics, studying across Lisbon, Paris, and Berlin through Forward College. Her studies focus on international political theory, security, and foreign policy, with a particular interest in how strategic narratives shape military interventions and global decision-making. This interest has been developed through fieldwork in Vietnam and Ghana, where she explored how legacies of conflict and perceptions of development influence political legitimacy and civilian resilience. She later worked with the Sustainable and Interoperable Digital Identity (SIDI) Hub on governance and displacement, assisting the organisation at the 2025 Internet Governance Forum. Alongside her academic work, Marie has gained hands-on experience through humanitarian support roles with the Norwegian Red Cross and field-based research in regions shaped by the long-term impacts of conflict. These grassroots experiences continue to shape her curiosity about diplomacy, democratic governance, and the human dimensions of international security.
members.uni: London School of Economics, Forward College
members.companies: Sustainable and Interoperable Digital Identity (SIDI) Hub, Norwegian Red Cross
members.interests: International political theory, Strategic narratives, Military interventions, Civilian resilience, Diplomacy

members.name: Adam Hermann
members.bio: Adam Hermann is currently pursuing a master's degree in Space Science and Technology at Aalto University. His academic and professional interests are centered on space technology, with a particular focus on the geopolitical implications and strategic importance of the space sector. These interests are not only theoretical; Adam actively applies his knowledge through his engagement with the Space Generation Advisory Council (SGAC), where he contributes to discussions and initiatives shaping the future of space industry. Additionally, he has gained hands-on experience by participating in engineering projects such as Aalto-3, a student-led satellite mission that underscores his commitment to practical innovation in space technology. Adam is driven by a research-oriented approach, combining a strong technical background with a passion for addressing complex challenges at the intersection of technology and international relations.
members.interests: Space technology, Geopolitical space implications, Strategic space sector, Practical space innovation

members.name: Matteo Minafra
members.bio: Matteo Minafra is a Bachelor's student in International Politics and Government at Bocconi University, aiming to specialise in European governance, diplomacy, and transnational policy. As a researcher and board member within a diplomacy association, he actively contributes to analytical work on international relations and institutional cooperation. A work he fostered also as the lead of the geopolitical section within a cultural association he helped grow in the past two years. Matteo's interests center on the evolving architecture of European integration, focusing on the development of a common European defence identity and the role of industries in the sector in achieving strategic autonomy. He is particularly committed to exploring how research, innovation, and industrial cooperation in the defence sector can enhance Europe's security capabilities and reinforce the political and technological foundations of European cohesion.
members.interests: European governance, Transnational policy, European defence identity, Strategic autonomy, Industrial cooperation

members.name: Natalya Hoare
members.bio: Natalya Hoare is a Bachelor's student in English Literature at The University of Edinburgh with an ambition to qualify as a lawyer after her degree. Her position on the Defence Commission combines her interest in the international legal field, regarding both state geopolitics and cross border commercial law, with a passion for the defence sector. As a member of her University Officer Training Corps (CEUOTC), Natalya is regularly able to develop her leadership skills in a military training environment and has also gained knowledge/training in the law of armed conflict. Her writing and analytical skills developed from her degree have also been utilised in various journalistic writing including political articles written throughout her education and with the news desk at DMG Media, London, in 2024 where she was published multiple times in the i Paper. Her goal is to apply her analytical skills and unique training experiences to the researching and evaluation of military law, commercial law and global geopolitics. She is specifically interested in the new challenges facing the European defence market and how the military legal sector must adapt as a consequence.
members.companies: City of Edinburgh University Officer Training Corps (CEUOTC), DMG Media, The i Paper
members.interests: International legal field, Cross border commercial law, Military law, Law of armed conflict, Global geopolitics

members.name: Miguel Daza Céspedes
members.bio: Miguel Daza Céspedes is a final-year student completing a Double Bachelor's in Business Analytics and International Relations at Universidad Pontificia Comillas (ICADE) in Madrid. His work sits at the intersection of quantitative analysis and European security policy, with a particular focus on nuclear deterrence and proliferation dynamics. His research centres on how U.S. military interventions shaped the strategic calculus of non-nuclear states; arguing that the fates of Iraq and Libya signalled to regimes worldwide that nuclear capability represents the only reliable guarantee of survival against external coercion. This comparative framework informs his broader interest in how deterrence theory intersects with contemporary questions of European strategic autonomy and great power competition. He has built a professional background spanning data analytics, geopolitical risk analysis, quantitative finance, and cybersecurity consulting, including work on cross-sector engagement projects aligned with Saudi Vision 2030 at Metyis. He is also the developer of MERIDIAN, an independent OSINT platform integrating geospatial intelligence, supply chain monitoring, and disinformation detection, a project that reflects his commitment to bridging the gap between data-driven methods and strategic decision-making. Miguel will pursue the MA in War Studies at King's College London.
members.uni: Universidad Pontificia Comillas (ICADE), King's College London
members.field_of_studies: Business Analytics, International Relations, War Studies
members.interests: Nuclear deterrence, Proliferation dynamics, Quantitative analysis, European security policy, Geopolitical risk analysis

members.name: Nigel Pang
members.bio: Nigel Pang is a first year BSc International Relations student at the London School of Economics and Political Science. His main interests are focused in maritime security, the proliferation of unmanned and digital weapons, especially in its use within gray-zone warfare. These interests have been honed as an officer in the Singapore Navy, assuming appointments on surface vessels and combat diving units. As a Speaker Officer in the LSESU Grimshaw Club of International Relations, he has organised high-level engagement events surrounding the adoption of artificial intelligence among other fledgling technologies and their impact on trade, security and global interdependence. Notably, he hopes to further understand, develop and contribute to opportunities for cooperation between European and Southeast Asian defence and security partners.
members.uni: London School of Economics and Political Science
members.interests: Maritime security, Gray-zone warfare, Unmanned weapons, Artificial intelligence, Euro-ASEAN cooperation

members.name: Ines Bellumore
members.bio: Ines Bellumore is a Bachelor's student in Global Law at Bocconi University. She aims to specialise in defence and operational research to pursue a career in international organisations. She takes part in various diplomacy-oriented academic associations and focuses on the study of conflicts across the world. She believes that addressing today's global challenges requires a comprehensive understanding of cultures, legal systems, and economic dynamics. Her academic interests lie at the intersection of international law, security, and strategic analysis, with particular attention to the legal and political dynamics of armed conflicts. Through her involvement in student-led initiatives and collaborative projects, she engages with contemporary global challenges and develops a multidisciplinary perspective on crisis management and international cooperation. Driven by a strong interest in geopolitics and institutional decision-making, she seeks to contribute to research and policy discussions that address evolving security threats and promote sustainable peace.

Her academic path combines a strong quantitative foundation in economic theory with a growing focus on financial systems and European economic governance. Finally, she hopes to pursue a career in the private financial sector, where she aims to contribute to responsible, forward-looking investment strategies that reflect both economic opportunity and societal challenges.

As Head of the Energy Commission at VOYCE, he leads discussions and research on European energy policy and system transformation. He aims to contribute to Europe's energy transition by bridging technical innovation, renewable integration, and effective policy, promoting an understanding of sustainability not as a burden but as a pathway to economic resilience and long-term social well-being.

members.bio: Dmitriy Genchev is a Bachelors student at Bocconi University pursuing a degree in Economics and Management. He is passionate about geo-politics and economics, as well as their relationship to the energy security of the European Union. Specifically, he is interested in the future of de-coupling with Russia and securing new energy agreements, as well as public policy remedies to decrease current energy dependencies. Outside his activity within VOYCE, Dmitriy works for the Global Academy for Future Governance and is an analyst for the Bocconi association, Aleph. Additionally, he is the President of the Bocconi Students for Literature and Humanities association, being passionate about promoting cultural engagement. He hopes to contribute to the preservation of an independent and united Europe and the furthering of the European project.

members.name: Maria Beatriz de Abreu Afonso
members.bio: After graduating in Communication Design from the Faculty of Fine Arts in Lisbon, Maria Beatriz has completed a Masters in Anthropology at the Nova University in 2022 with the thesis "Anthropology and the invisible: the decolonization of anthropological thought through poetry". Since 2020, she has been writing and presenting several collections of poetry and she has written for artists, while working as a creative copywriter at McCann Lisbon. In September 2023, she began her PhD in Anthropology with a focus on Artistic Practices. There, she joined IFIL-Nova's "Mapping Philosophy as a Way of Life" research project, where she wrote the article "Spiritual exercises beyond feminism: meditations on Simone Weil". In 2025, she joined CRIA - Centro em Rede de Investigação em Antropologia. Her PhD research aims to provide a space to imagine new utopias while exploring different ontologies and methodologies with indigenous artists from Brazil. She believes we are able to change reality, as long as we do not give up on hoping, imagining and commit to finding a better one.

members.bio: Carlotta Ferracina is an Italian student that has lived in Paris, Zurich, Miami, and Singapore, an experience that shaped her interest for global affairs, cultural diversity, and human rights. She is currently in South Korea studying Political Science and International Relations at Yonsei University. Carlotta has a strong commitment to social change and justice, she is active in volunteering with Libera Italia, an NGO that focuses on combatting the mafia/organised crime, corruption, and systemic injustice. Carlotta is particularly passionate about human rights advocacy, with a focus on marginalized communities and the intersection of policy and social justice. Her international background continues to influence her academic and volunteer work, reinforcing her belief in cross-cultural collaboration as a force for meaningful political change.
members.interests: Global affairs diversity, Human rights advocacy, Organized crime combat, Social justice policy, Cross-cultural collaboration

members.name: Edoardo Nepi
members.bio: Edoardo Nepi is starting his second year at Gabriele D'Annunzio University, where he is studying linguistic mediation and intercultural communication. He is particularly interested in how international relations are shaped by geopolitics, politics, mediation, and cross-cultural exchange. He studied at the Oslo School of Architecture and Design (AHO) in Norway for two years, which expanded his understanding of the world and strengthened his appreciation for intercultural communication. He turned his attention to languages after returning to Italy, where he cultivated a strong command of the language and a strong dedication to intercultural understanding. Edoardo aspires to work within the European Union, contributing to diplomacy, policy, and cultural cooperation. His academic path and international background reflect his dedication to building bridges between communities in an increasingly interconnected world.
members.uni: Gabriele D'Annunzio University, Oslo School of Architecture and Design (AHO)
members.interests: Geopolitical mediation, Intercultural communication dynamics, Linguistic diplomacy, Cultural cooperation bridges

members.name: Gaïa Molinaro
members.bio: Gaïa Molinaro is a French-Italian student starting her second year of BSc in Economics and Social Sciences at Bocconi University. She is drawn to political sciences and geopolitics since her 3-year experience gained as a delegate at the Model United Nations in Geneva. Determined and passionate, she is deeply convinced that her generation needs to take ownership of their future and can make a difference. She believes in the value of building a stronger Europe and considers European identity as an essential foundation. Gaïa is experienced in various forms of art; she has been practicing dance in competitions since the age of 4, individually and in teams. As a result, she understands the power of culture and the importance of it to federate a united society. She hopes to pursue a career as a diplomat in order to bring people together and align them around shared ideas.
members.interests: Political sciences geopolitics, European identity foundations, Cultural diplomacy, Arts and society

members.name: Ginevra Savarè
members.bio: Ginevra Savarè is from Italy and currently in her third year of studies in International Politics and Government at Bocconi University. She is particularly interested in the future of liberal democracy and the role of young generations in shaping political change. For this reason, she is part of VOYCE, where she is engaged in research and policy analysis on European affairs and economics. She believes that rigorous economic analysis and political vision must go hand in hand. A strong and united Europe requires evidence-based policies, institutional responsibility, and the active engagement of the younger generation. Through her work, she aims to contribute to a more resilient, forward-looking, and democratic Europe.
members.interests: Liberal democracy, Youth political change, European affairs, Policy analysis

members.name: Margot Padilla
members.bio: Margot Padilla is a French master's graduate in International Relations from Luiss Guido Carli University in Rome. She has an academic background shaped by studies across Montpellier, Budapest, and Brussels, with a focus on diplomacy, European governance, and global economics. She has experience in communication and policy analysis, having worked at the United Nations and in public affairs. Her work focuses on analyzing the European Union's external action from an economic perspective and understanding its role in global affairs.
members.interests: Diplomacy, European governance, Global economics, EU external action

members.name: Naveen Sivakumar
members.bio: Naveen is a researcher of political economics and development who studied economics at Bocconi University. He is currently researching structural inequality and the intergenerational transmission of poverty in the EU. He was formerly the President of Aleph Analisi Strategiche, Italy's leading student think tank, and has publication experience on international relations and political economics, primarily in Asia.
members.where_from: India (Implied by name, but no country explicitly specified in text)
members.interests: Structural inequality, Intergenerational poverty, Political economics, International relations

members.name: Maria Yankova
members.bio: Maria Yankova is from Bulgaria and is currently pursuing a degree in Economics and Management at Bocconi University in Milan. She is particularly interested in the political dimensions of economics, focusing on how institutions, governance, and policy decisions shape economic outcomes. Her work explores the interplay between economic systems and political structures, with an emphasis on how decision-making influence economic growth and stability.
members.interests: Political economics, Institutional governance, Economic growth stability, Policy decision-making

members.name: Maria Dimitrova
members.bio: Maria Dimitrova is from Bulgaria and is currently pursuing a degree in International Economics and Finance at Bocconi University in Milan. She is particularly interested in behavioral economics, with a focus on how individuals react to policies and economic shocks. She also explores issues of inequality and differences of economic development within the European Union - how it arises and how it affects the mindsets of people.
members.interests: Behavioral economics, Policy reaction, EU inequality, Economic development mindsets

members.name: Angelica Bareggi
members.bio: Angelica Bareggi is currently a second-year student in Economics and Social Sciences at Bocconi University. Her academic interests focus on the intersection of economic policy and long-term competitiveness, with particular attention to Europe's capacity to strengthen its economic resilience in an evolving geopolitical landscape. She is especially interested in how policy and economics can be leveraged as tools to support sustainable growth, recognizing that many of Europe's most pressing challenges, such as preserving its social model and financing the green and digital transitions, depend on the strength and adaptability of its economic base. Her work centers on understanding how productivity, innovation, and effective policy design can reinforce the European Union's ability to remain competitive in an evolving global landscape.
members.where_from: Italy (Implied by name/location, no country explicitly specified)
members.interests: Economic policy, Long-term competitiveness, Sustainable growth, Green digital transition, Policy design

members.name: Riccardo Mencarelli
members.bio: Riccardo Mencarelli is an Italian student pursuing a Bachelor's degree in International Economics and Management at Bocconi University. He's interested in understanding how institutions and policies can address social inequalities and expand opportunities across Europe. Alongside his studies, he has gained experience through youth education, volunteering, and other initiatives related to civic engagement.
members.interests: Social inequalities, European institutional policy, Youth education, Civic engagement

members.name: Francesco Sottero
members.bio: Francesco Sottero is from Italy and is currently pursuing a degree in Economics and Computer Science at the University of Milan. During an exchange semester at Singapore Management University and his travels across Asia, he developed a deep interest in monetary policy and economic development. He is now focused on using his background in programming and data analytics to evaluate and analyze economic policies. To further develop his skills, Francesco will join the MSc in Economics and Social Sciences at Bocconi University beginning next year.
members.uni: University of Milan, Singapore Management University, Bocconi University
members.interests: Monetary policy, Economic development, Policy data analytics, Programming applications

members.name: Silvia Dipalma
members.bio: Silvia Dipalma is currently completing a double degree in International Management at Bocconi University and ESSEC Business School. She has always seen politics and economics as inseparable, a belief that grew stronger after a semester at the Hong Kong Polytechnic University, where she wrote her thesis on the assertion of an independent Hongkonger identity and its role in the 2019 protests. She had the opportunity to intern at the European Commission's DG ECFIN, working on IMF reform and G20 coordination, which allowed her to engage with questions of global macroeconomics and trade imbalances from the inside. She is also passionate about development economics and climate finance, two areas she believes will define much of what Europe needs to confront in the years ahead. She joined VOYCE because she believes rigorous analysis and political vision belong together, and she is excited to contribute to that work there.
members.where_from: Italy (Implied by name/location, no country explicitly specified)
members.uni: Bocconi University, ESSEC Business School, Hong Kong Polytechnic University
members.interests: Global macroeconomics, IMF G20 reform, Trade imbalances, Climate finance, Political identity

members.name: Giovanni Della Rocca
members.bio: Giovanni Della Rocca is an Italian student pursuing a Bachelor's in Economics and Social Sciences at Bocconi University in Milan, with an academic background shaped by studies in Boston, United States. His interests center on public policy and development economics, with a particular focus on wealth inequality and redistribution mechanisms, looking at how economic systems create and deepen disparities between social groups and generations. His work aims to better understand the roots of inequality in the European Union and how policy can address it.
members.interests: Wealth inequality, Redistribution mechanisms, Public policy, Development economics

members.name: Conor Shields
members.bio: Conor Shields is from Scotland and is currently pursuing a degree in Economics at the University of St Andrews. He is particularly interested in international trade and development economics, having completed his dissertation on the economic impact of the Russia-Ukraine war on export flows from the Baltic states. Furthermore, he is passionate about the economic future of Scotland and its relationship with the EU. He is currently investigating the potential economic impact of Scottish independence, and its impact on Scotland's relations with the EU.
members.interests: International trade, Development economics, Trade conflict impact, Scottish independence economics

members.name: Giulio M. Boggetti
members.bio: Giulio M. Boggetti is a third-year student at Bocconi University, pursuing a B.Sc. in International Politics and Government. His interests lie at the intersection of European politics, diplomacy, war and the governance of emerging technologies. He most recently worked at FleishmanHillard EU as a lobbyist in Brussels, advising Fortune 500 tech and fintech clients on key European digital files through stakeholder mapping, in-person monitoring of European Parliament proceedings, and weekly policy briefs. Earlier, he interned at the Bank of Italy, contributing to the Digital Euro initiative and leading a team focused on its integration into Italian public life. At VOYCE, Giulio serves as the Commissioner of Foreign Affairs, where he leads the team's research agenda and oversees the drafting of policy reports and articles on the geopolitical questions most relevant to the EU. Most recently he is authoring a comprehensive report on the economic effect of war refugees in Europe. Outside his academic and professional commitments, he is a passionate alpinist, climber, and traveler drawn to the cultures and ideas that shape the international affairs he studies.
members.interests: European politics diplomacy, Emerging technology governance, Tech fintech lobbying, Geopolitical research

members.name: Giulio Draghetti
members.bio: Giulio Draghetti is currently pursuing a Bachelor of Science in International Economics and Finance at Università Bocconi, focusing on macroeconomics, geopolitics, and international relations. He is actively engaged in shaping European policy discourse as former Head of the Foreign Policy Commission at VOYCE, coordinating the creation of policy papers and organizing international workshops in collaboration with influential stakeholders. Additionally, Giulio contributes to strategic analysis and events with Italy's leading student think tank, Aleph Analisi Strategiche. Giulio will be working at the World Bank this Summer.
members.companies: VOYCE, Aleph Analisi Strategiche, World Bank
members.interests: Macroeconomics geopolitics, International relations discourse, Strategic analysis papers, Stakeholder workshops

members.name: Constantin Tremmel
members.bio: Constantin Tremmel, is in his third year of law studies at the Ludwig Maximilians Universität in Munich. AS a scholarship holder of the Friedrich Naumann Foundation for Freedom, he is deeply committed to liberal values and the idea of a strong, sovereign, and united Europe. This belief guides both his academic path and his civic engagement - for instance, through his voluntary work supporting refugees, he advocates for reform-oriented politics that respect the voice of the younger generation. We are not just the future - we are part of the present. Let us shape a better Europe together.
members.interests: Liberal political values, Reform oriented politics, Youth civic engagement, Sovereign Europe frameworks

members.name: Gabriele Mammarella
members.bio: Gabriele Mammarella is currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Economics and Management at Bocconi University in Milan, where he is actively engaged in initiatives related to strategic analysis, finance, and geopolitics. He serves as a Research Fellow in the Foreign Policy Commission at VOYCE. He has a strong interest in international affairs, innovation, and public policy, alongside a deep passion for the entrepreneurial ecosystem. He is committed to continuously improving his skills and contributing to a more integrated, effective, and cohesive European Union. Gabriele believes that the challenges of the new decade require pragmatism and a multidisciplinary approach, and he strives to contribute by fostering informed debate among policymakers and the broader public, with a view to advancing deeper and more efficient European integration.
members.interests: International affairs innovation, Entrepreneurial ecosystems, Multidisciplinary public policy, European integration debate

members.name: Oscar Eveno
members.bio: Oscar Eveno is a bachelor student at Bocconi University, pursuing a double diploma with HEC Paris in International Government and Data Analysis. His interests lie in international affairs and political research. Beyond VOYCE, Oscar also contributes to research and policy analysis in other geopolitical associations, such as Politeia or Bocconi Students for Diplomacy and International Cooperation.
members.companies: Politeia, Bocconi Students for Diplomacy and International Cooperation
members.interests: International affairs, Political research, Geopolitical analysis

members.name: Leonardo Beria
members.bio: Leonardo Beria is a student of Economics and Management at Bocconi University and founder and co-host of a podcast at Radio Bocconi, where he covers economics, politics and current affairs. He is a Research Fellow in the Foreign Policy Commission at VOYCE, producing analytical articles on EU policy and geopolitics, translating complex macro and strategic issues into clear frameworks and practical insights. He believes in European integration as a project that carries forward the vision of its founding principles, promoting cooperation, stability and freedom in an increasingly complex global landscape.
members.interests: EU policy, Geopolitics, Macro frameworks, European integration

members.name: Lia Bassanini
members.bio: Lia Bassanini is a French-Italian student passionate about all issues related to human rights, especially migration. After obtaining her BSc in International Politics and Government at Bocconi University, Milan, in 2025, she went on to pursue her studies at the Graduate Institute, Geneva, where she is focusing on international and development studies, specialising in Human Rights. Her goal is to work in NGOs or IOs focusing on migration-related topics. To further pursue her interests, she worked for 2 months as a member of the legal team of the Italian Council for Refugees. She then did a 4-months research internship at Fondazione Ing. Rodolfo Debenedetti under the supervision of Prof. Tito Boeri. She then interned an the Food and Agriculture Organisation, in the Statistics Division, further practicing and strengthening her data analysis and policy evaluation skills.
members.field_of_studies: International Politics and Government, International and Development Studies, Human Rights
members.companies: Italian Council for Refugees, Fondazione Ing. Rodolfo Debenedetti, Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO)
members.interests: Human rights, Migration topics, Development studies, Policy evaluation

members.name: Clément Levrat
members.bio: Clément Levrat is a Swiss-French student entering the first year of his Master's degree in European Affairs at the Université Libre de Bruxelles. During his Bachelor's studies in Political Science and International Development at McGill University, Clément developed a strong interest in migration policy, human rights, and international affairs. Outside VOYCE, he is actively involved in several extracurricular activities related to these fields, such as volunteering with Amnesty International. After completing his studies, he aspires to pursue a career within European institutions, where he hopes to contribute to shaping their future direction.
members.uni: Université Libre de Bruxelles, McGill University
members.field_of_studies: European Affairs, Political Science, International Development
members.interests: Migration policy, Human rights, International affairs, European institutions

members.name: Keyan Roubaie
members.bio: Keyan Roubaie is a British-born Iranian-Iraqi postgraduate student at King's College London, where he specialises in the political economy of the Middle East. With a background in International Relations and fluency in English, French, and Farsi, Keyan's work is grounded in cross-cultural communication and global policy engagement. His research explores protest narratives, informal governance, and the political dynamics of displacement and migration, particularly within authoritarian and conflict-affected regions. Having worked closely with French and Farsi-speaking communities, Keyan brings an intercultural insight into his policy advocacy, rooted in both academic study and professional experiences across Europe and MENA. He hopes to anchor his advocacy skills to engage in inclusive dialogue, contribute to policy forums and support migrant and diaspora communities by amplifying their voices, connecting lived experiences to broader political structures, and fostering collaborative spaces for empowerment.
members.field_of_studies: Political Economy of the Middle East, International Relations
members.interests: Protest narratives, Displacement and migration, Cross-cultural communication, Diaspora communities advocacy

members.name: Antonino Enrico Repaci
members.bio: Antonino Enrico Repaci is an Italian student with a strong curiosity about how politics, policy, and diplomacy shape Europe from within. He completed a BSc in International Politics and Government at Bocconi University in July 2025 and began an MSc in European and International Politics and Policy at the London School of Economics the following September. To further pursue his interests, Antonino interned at the Italian Ministry of Justice, where he worked on EU cohesion policy, drafting a research report based on European legal documents and statistical data. He then completed an eight-month internship at Magic Amor ETS as a Junior Analyst in international cooperation, where he analyzed EU policies on international cooperation and development and wrote multiple research papers. Overall, Antonino hopes to build a career in EU diplomacy, where he can help shape policies that make European institutions more democratic, cohesive, and globally engaged.
members.uni: Bocconi University, London School of Economics (LSE)
members.field_of_studies: International Politics and Government, European and International Politics and Policy
members.companies: Italian Ministry of Justice, Magic Amor ETS
members.interests: EU cohesion policy, International cooperation, EU diplomacy, Institutional democratic design

members.name: Tomás Consonni
members.bio: Tomás Consonni is an Italian-Brazilian student with a strong interest in the relationship between economics and politics in Europe. He is currently in his third year of the International Politics and Government program at Bocconi University. He is particularly drawn to research on topics such as inequality, migration, and causal inference. He regularly engages with economic and political debates and deepens his understanding through academic work and personal study. He aims to further develop his research skills and contribute to addressing policy challenges in Europe in the future.
members.interests: Economics and politics, Inequality studies, Migration tracking, Causal inference analysis

members.name: Agnese Colotta
members.bio: Agnese Colotta is an Italian student heading into her third year at Maastricht University, pursuing an LLB in European Law. She has a strong interest in European and international law, with a particular focus on social justice, migration, human rights, and democracy. Beyond her studies and her involvement in VOYCE's Immigration Commission, she is also a writer for the Maastricht Journal of Politics and Economics, producing articles on politics, economics, and global issues. She has a passion for writing and hopes to pursue a career in international law or public policy.
members.companies: Maastricht Journal of Politics and Economics
members.interests: European law, Social justice, Migration human rights, Public policy writing

members.name: Rusa Malaguradze
members.bio: Rusa Malaguradze is a Georgian student of International Politics and Government at Bocconi University, in her final year. Her interests lie in migration, equality, and political economy, with a particular focus on how these issues shape European integration. Alongside her studies, she is a member of “12 Sartuli”, a newly formed youth political movement in Georgia that stands in opposition to the current government and advocates for the country’s European future. She is also completing a creative communications internship at More is Love, a Georgian fashion brand, reflecting her passion for fashion and cultural expression.
members.interests: Migration and equality, Political economy, European integration, Creative communications

members.name: Sinem Özbal
members.bio: Sinem Özbal is a Norwegian-Turkish Politics & International Relations student at the London School of Economics, studying across Lisbon, Paris, and Berlin through Forward College. She has a strong interest in international security and the interaction between state interests and global governance challenges. Alongside her studies, her experience is grounded in cross-cultural communication and humanitarian engagement, shaped through several volunteer roles and leadership positions, including her involvement in ANSA (Association of Norwegian Students Abroad), where she contributed to institutional collaboration and communication in a multi-cultural environment. Motivated by opportunities for cross-sector engagement, she seeks to foster global cooperation and strengthen humanitarian action and social justice, particularly in areas related to migration and children’s rights.
members.uni: London School of Economics, Forward College
members.interests: International security, Cross-cultural communication, Humanitarian action, Children rights migration

members.name: Filippo Negri
members.bio: Filippo is an Italian postgraduate in European and International Public Policy at the London School of Economics, having previously completed a BSc in International Politics and Government at Bocconi University. He is currently working for a political monitoring firm in the United Kingdom, where he supports clients in navigating the political and policy landscape. He aspires to continue a career in public affairs, with a strong interest in evidence-based policy analysis and a particular focus on labour markets and welfare states. Through his academic background and professional experience, he aims to contribute to informed social sciences policy-making grounded in empirical evidence.
members.uni: London School of Economics (LSE), Bocconi University
members.field_of_studies: European and International Public Policy, International Politics and Government
members.interests: Public affairs, Evidence-based policy, Labour markets, Welfare states dynamics

members.name: David Malacarne
members.bio: David Malacarne is an Italian graduate of the LSE–Bocconi double degree in Public Policy and Policy Analysis, where he specialised in labour, migration, and welfare economics, with a strong focus on applied microeconometrics. Alongside his studies, David has gained extensive research experience at Bocconi University, the University of Birmingham, and UC Berkeley. His work spans a range of topics, including migration and labour market dynamics, public safety, AI-driven job displacement, education, and social policy evaluation. In the long term, David aims to pursue a career as an economist focused on the evaluation of public policies, with the goal of informing more effective and equitable policy design.
members.uni: London School of Economics (LSE), Bocconi University, University of Birmingham, UC Berkeley
members.field_of_studies: Public Policy and Policy Analysis, Economics
members.companies: Bocconi University, University of Birmingham, UC Berkeley
members.interests: Applied microeconometrics, Labour migration economics, AI job displacement, Public policy design

members.name: Egemen Aray
members.bio: Egemen is a Turkish master’s student in Social Sciences at the University of Chicago, where he is concentrating in Political Science and pursuing a Graduate Certificate in Computational Social Science. He obtained his bachelor’s degree in International Politics and Government from Bocconi University, where he developed a background in European politics and economics and spent an exchange semester at Sciences Po. He has held multiple research, editorial, and policy positions, including research assistantships at Bocconi and Humboldt University, where he contributed to research on democracy and Islam in Indonesia and Turkey. Currently, in addition to serving as a Policy Adviser to the youth branch of Turkey’s main opposition party, the Republican People’s Party, he is also a Graduate Student Affiliate at the Chicago Center on Democracy, a Pritzker Fellow Ambassador at the University of Chicago Institute of Politics, and a Graduate Student Fellow at the International House. His interests include migration, gender, and democratic backsliding, with a geographical focus on Turkey, Europe, and the Middle East, and he ultimately aims to pursue a career in European affairs.
members.uni: University of Chicago, Bocconi University, Sciences Po, Humboldt University
members.field_of_studies: Social Sciences, Political Science, International Politics and Government
members.companies: Republican People’s Party (Turkey), Chicago Center on Democracy, University of Chicago Institute of Politics
members.interests: Computational social science, Democratic backsliding, Migration and gender, European affairs

members.name: Anna Puricelli
members.bio: Anna Puricelli is an Italian student with a strong interest in the economic and social implications of migration. She is currently in her second year of the Master’s degree in Economics and Social Sciences at Bocconi University and is currently a visiting student at the SMU School of Economics in Singapore. She is particularly drawn to research on how migration shapes labor markets, productivity, and long-term economic growth. Her interest in this field stems from its crucial role in shaping and transforming many countries, such as Italy, as well as from a desire to bring clarity to a topic that is often discussed superficially and without sufficient empirical evidence.
members.uni: Bocconi University, SMU School of Economics Singapore
members.interests: Migration economic implications, Labor market productivity, Empirical economic evidence, Long-term growth

members.name: Paulius Danielius
members.bio: Paulius Danielius is a Lithuanian undergraduate student currently studying Economic and Social Sciences at Bocconi University in Milan. He is in the process of developing his research and writing skills while building a strong foundation of knowledge across a variety of fields. He seeks to integrate these perspectives into his analysis of migration in the EU. While he often considers the broader picture, he believes that case studies of successful small-scale initiatives can serve as viable models for wider application. In the long term, Paulius aims to make a positive impact through his research and writing, critically examining flawed policies and contributing to the development of better ones.
members.interests: EU migration analysis, Small-scale initiatives, Policy critical examination, Research and writing

members.name: Ilaria Ronconi
members.bio: Ilaria Ronconi is an Italian graduate in European Law from Utrecht University (2025) and, before that, from a Bachelor's degree in International, European and Comparative Law at the University of Trento. Her interests lie in European law, fundamental rights and external relations, with a particular focus on EU asylum law. Outside VOYCE, she is currently pursuing an internship at the Research Centre of the Municipality of Genoa, where she works on policy documents and EU project reviews, and is a published author in the European Foreign Affairs Review. In the coming years, she hopes to obtain a PhD in European Law and to pursue a career in research at the institutional level.
members.field_of_studies: European Law, International, European and Comparative Law
members.companies: Research Centre of the Municipality of Genoa, European Foreign Affairs Review
members.interests: EU asylum law, Fundamental rights, Policy document review, Institutional research

members.name: Maddalena Vigo
members.bio: Maddalena Vigo is a Law student at Bocconi University. Through her studies, she has developed a strong interest in European Law and Comparative Law, and is particularly fascinated by how legal systems and instruments can be leveraged to promote justice, equality, and democratic values across borders. She is a strong believer in cross-border cooperation and in the value of an interdisciplinary approach—convinced that legal analysis must also consider economic and global perspectives to be truly effective. She joined VOYCE’s mission of bridging the gap between European policymaking and the voices of young people across the continent. As Head of the Legal Affairs Commission at VOYCE, she coordinates a uniquely diverse team of law students and young professionals from across multiple European jurisdictions engaged in researching and analysing how to nurture the European project through jurisdiction, fundamental rights and legal knowledge.
members.interests: European legal systems, Comparative law frameworks, Cross-border judicial cooperation, Interdisciplinary legal analysis

members.name: Estella Neumayr
members.bio: Estella Neumayr is a third-year Law student at the University of Warwick, pursuing a double degree in English and German Law. She is currently completing her year abroad at Freie Universität Berlin. Through the comparative nature of her studies, she has developed a strong interest in European and comparative legal frameworks, particularly in how legal systems interact across jurisdictions. Building on both her academic background and practical experience in governmental work, including experience within a European affairs department, Estella has cultivated a particular passion for European Law and its role in shaping cross-border cooperation and legal integration. She is especially interested in exploring the relationship between national and supranational legal systems and aims to contribute a comparative perspective to legal research and discourse.
members.uni: University of Warwick, Freie Universität Berlin
members.interests: Comparative legal frameworks, Supranational legal integration, National legal systems, Cross-border legal discourse

members.name: Laura Miró Pellicer
members.bio: Laura is a second-year Law student at King's College London, pursuing a double degree in English and Spanish Law. She is especially passionate about issues concerning international legal cooperation, access to justice and the relationship between EU institutions and the citizens they serve. Moreover, she is eager to bring a comparative perspective to legal research and advocacy. As a member of the Legal Affairs Commission at VOYCE, she looks forward to contributing to cross-border research projects that explore the legitimacy and harmony of EU law, with a focus on aligning institutional actions with the Union's foundational values. By combining academic insight, practical experience, and a strong commitment to social impact, she is hoping to contribute to VOYCE's mission of shaping a more just and united European legal landscape.
members.interests: International legal cooperation, Access to justice, EU institutional legitimacy, Cross-border legal research

members.name: Magdalena Georgieva
members.bio: Magdalena Georgieva is a second-year Bulgarian student at Bocconi University, enrolled in the Bachelor of Global Law. Her dream is to work as an IP/IT lawyer at the European level and to represent her country as a legislator in the European Commission, working alongside those who drafted the AI Act. Her passion for law sparked her interest in the regulation of AI and led her to the conclusion that technology is what truly drives innovation and progress. For her, the intersection of law and technology is a sphere that is only beginning to develop, and she wants to be part of this evolution by conducting academic research on the legal regulation of AI. This summer, she is interning at one of the first AI-native platforms, which automates legal research, document review, and drafting. Outside of university, she is passionate about adventure sports such as mountain biking, trail running, and open-water swimming. She also practiced ballet for nine years.
members.interests: AI legal regulation, IP/IT european law, Automated document review, Innovation law framework

members.name: Vansh Minocha
members.bio: Vansh Minocha is a Bachelor's student in Law and Sociology at the University of Warwick. His foundation in criminal law, shaped through his service with the Singapore Police Force, progressed to a broader interest in legal policy, technological governance, and comparative legal systems. His writing explores the intersection of innovation and regulation, particularly in fast-moving areas like AI, digital infrastructure, and global governance. Having lived across India, Singapore, Hong Kong, and the UK, Vansh brings a cross-cultural perspective to legal questions. He is especially focused on how law responds to societal and technological change, and how regulatory frameworks can be made more agile, coherent, and inclusive.
members.interests: Technological governance, Comparative legal systems, AI regulatory agility, Digital infrastructure policy

members.name: Margherita Carboni
members.bio: Margherita Carboni is currently pursuing a combined Bachelor's and Master's degree in Law at the University of Pisa, Italy. Although still at the beginning of her studies, she has recently developed a strong interest in European Law and Space Law, as well as Contract Law, fascination sparked by her experience as a Business and Legal Associate at JEVIS, Pisa's Junior Enterprise. Part of VOYCE's Legal Affairs commission, she's eager to support initiatives that promote meaningful social impact, and she values being part of a purpose-driven community where she can give her best and learn from others striving for the same.
members.interests: European space law, International contract law, Junior enterprise frameworks, Social impact policy

members.name: Teo Pizzati
members.bio: Teo is a third-year Psychology student at Rome's Sapienza University. He aspire to become both a therapist and an academic researcher. His studies focus on Developmental and Social/Political Psychology, with a particular interest in integrating Dynamic Psychology with Neuroscience and Cognitive Psychology. He's driven by the conviction that European regulations must evolve to safeguard individual and collective well-being, considering the intense technological changes shaping our lives. He strongly believes this is only achievable through innovative EU regulations, and this is why he is part of VOYCE.
members.interests: Social political psychology, Technological lifestyle impacts, Cognitive psychology integration, Well-being safeguard regulations

members.name: Aldo Fittante
members.bio: Aldo is a fourth-year Law student at Università Bocconi with a strong dedication to European legal integration, institutional legitimacy, and the evolving role of justice within the EU. As Head of the Legal Affairs Commission at VOYCE, he coordinates a uniquely diverse team of law students and young professionals from across multiple European jurisdictions. This multicultural legal ecosystem allows the Commission to explore the EU's legal and governance architecture from multiple perspectives: enhancing the legitimacy of its institutional framework, interpreting the evolving body of ECJ case-law, and evaluating the coherence between EU action and its foundational Treaties. Through a collaborative and research-driven approach, the Commission works to ensure that the European legal order remains firmly anchored in justice, fundamental rights, and...
members.interests: European legal integration, Institutional framework legitimacy, ECJ case law interpretation, Foundational treaty coherence

members.name: Nicola Povinelli
members.bio: Nicola Povinelli is a Law student at Bocconi University with strong interests in Corporate Law, Antitrust Law, and Tax Law. He is particularly drawn to the way legal frameworks shape markets and ensure economic fairness within an increasingly interconnected European system. By joining VOYCE, he embraced its mission to cut the gap between European policymaking and the voices of young people, driven by his conviction that a deeper European integration is both a strategic necessity in the current global landscape and a fundamental step toward safeguarding rights and protecting citizens.
members.interests: Corporate antitrust law, European tax systems, Market regulatory frameworks, Economic fairness integration

members.name: Cecilia de Peitl
members.bio: Cecilia de Peitl is a Bocconi Law student specialising in EU and international law through the THEMIS programme at Maastricht University, with a focus on how legal systems adapt to rapid technological change. She is particularly interested in how EU law can balance innovation, fundamental rights, and accountability, especially in digital rights, cybersecurity, and the legal implications of AI. She brings a precise, pragmatic approach to legal analysis and drafting, and thrives in multicultural, cross-border environments. She joined VOYCE's mission to strengthen dialogue between European policymaking and the voices of young people across the continent. As a member of VOYCE's Legal Commission, she contributes to rigorous, constructive discussion, while sharing ideas clearly and listening openly.
members.interests: Digital rights frameworks, Cybersecurity legal policy, AI legal implications, Technological legal adaptation

members.name: Jasmine Sabbatini
members.bio: Jasmine Sabbatini is an International Business Law LLM student at Queen Mary, University of London, and LLB Law graduate with hands-on experience across Italian, EU, and English jurisdictions. As Co-Founder and Outreach Officer of the Queen Mary European Affairs Society, she participated in events including Visit Europe House at the European Parliament Liaison Office in the United Kingdom. Multilingual in five languages, her background spans corporate compliance, cross-border M&A, and legal research at international law firms. Jasmine now brings this expertise to rigorous, accessible EU law commentary.
members.companies: Queen Mary European Affairs Society, International Law Firms
members.interests: Corporate compliance tracking, Cross border M&A law, European liaison operations, Multilingual legal research

members.name: Louise Tabary
members.bio: Louise is a French third-year student in law and political science at Sciences Po. She is interested in environmental and human rights law, as well as corporate responsibility, in particular with regards to polluting and digital companies. Next year, she will be pursuing a Master's in economic law in Paris, to better understand the law of markets and regulations, and how European law may contribute to a future in which human rights such as that to a healthy environment or to privacy are respected.
members.interests: Environmental human rights, Corporate social responsibility, Market regulation law, Economic law applications

members.name: Francesca Sacco
members.bio: Francesca Sacco is a fourth-year Italian student at Bocconi University in Milan, enrolled in the Bachelor of Law. Originally from Calabria, she has developed a strong academic interest in administrative and European law, with a particular focus on public policies, independent authorities, and the technical mechanisms that shape public law and governance. Her passion for politics and institutional dynamics has led her to explore how legal frameworks influence the functioning of public administration. She is especially interested in understanding and improving the systems governing public procurement, strategic behaviour, and public administrative procedures. Her dream is to become an administrative lawyer and contribute to reforming the system of public tenders and public administration, particularly in Southern Italy, making it more efficient, transparent, and responsive. Beyond law, she enjoys cinema, theatre, and exploring cultural spaces such as museums, exhibitions, and concerts.
members.interests: Administrative european law, Public procurement systems, Public administrative reform, Institutional tender transparency

members.name: Carlotta Fattor
members.bio: Carlotta Fattor is a Bachelor's student in Global Law at Bocconi University. She has developed a strong interest in European Union law and in how legal systems can respond to cross-border challenges while safeguarding fundamental rights and democratic values. Through her international experiences and multilingual background, she has cultivated a comparative and open-minded approach to legal studies. At VOYCE, she joined the Legal Affairs Commission to contribute to research and discussions on current EU legal developments, with the aim of making complex legal issues more accessible to young Europeans and fostering informed participation in European policymaking.
members.interests: EU cross border law, Democratic legal values, Complex law accessibility, European policymaking research

members.name: Sofia Montanino
members.bio: Sofia Montanino is a first year Master's student currently enrolled in the Bocconi–HEC Double Degree program in Economics and Social Sciences. Through her bachelor studies in Economics at Bocconi University, she has developed a strong interest in competition law and in how antitrust enforcement can safeguard fair competition and promote welfare. By joining the Legal Affairs Commission, she brings an economic perspective to legal analysis, drawing on microeconomic intuition to better understand incentives, strategic behaviour, and the broader effects of regulatory intervention. Through this interdisciplinary approach, she hopes to contribute to a deeper understanding of how European legal and regulatory frameworks can support fair, efficient, and well-functioning markets. She joined Voyce to be part of a community of young people that are eager to exchange ideas and perspectives and collaborate on projects that drive change.
members.interests: Competition law economics, Antitrust enforcement frameworks, Microeconomic legal analysis, Regulatory market intervention

members.name: Giada Grassi
members.bio: Giada Grassi is a member of the Legal Affairs team at VOYCE, where she serves as article writer. She is a fourth-year Law student at Bocconi University in Milan and is currently completing an exchange programme abroad. Alongside her studies, Giada is actively involved in the San Siro Legal Clinic, where she contributes to providing legal assistance and further strengthens her commitment to access to justice. She has a strong interest in sport and social initiatives, particularly in the way they intersect with law and community engagement.
members.interests: Access to justice clinics, Legal assistance research, Sports law intersection, Community social initiatives

members.name: Eleonora Rambelli
members.bio: Eleonora Rambelli is a third year student at the University of Trento, pursuing the Bachelor's Degree in Comparative, European and International Legal Studies (CEILS). Passionate about international law and security, she is experienced in editorial work and academic research projects.
members.field_of_studies: Comparative, European and International Legal Studies
members.interests: International security law, Comparative legal studies, Academic research editing

members.name: Andrea Casali
members.bio: Andrea Casali is a first year Master's student currently enrolled in Economics and Social Sciences at Bocconi university. He developed a keen interest in competition law and the antitrust measures implemented to preserve a competitive environment within the European Union, enabling both consumers and businesses to thrive. He joined the Legal Affairs Commission to assist in collecting and interpreting economic data while also drawing on his background in business economics to contribute to understanding when and why companies may engage in anti-competitive conduct and the incentives driving such behavior. He hopes to contribute to VOYCE's Legal Affairs Commission by collaborating with law students and combining their strengths to engage in in-depth discussions on European legislation.
members.interests: Antitrust data collection, Anti competitive behavior analysis, Business economics incentives, European legislation discussion

members.name: Tommaso Ferracina
members.bio: Tommaso Ferracina is an Italian student who spent most of his life abroad, living in Paris, Zurich, Miami, and Singapore. He completed his bachelor in Mathematical and Computing Sciences for Artificial Intelligence at Bocconi. Tommaso is passionate about open source technology (software and hardware), and is particularly interested in exploring the potential and risks of artificial intelligence. In August 2024, he co-founded Quercia Dev, an AI/ML research group that helps companies investigate promising areas they lack the resources to explore internally. With Quercia, he also contributed to several open-source projects, with a special focus on tools for personal productivity tracking and self-analysis. Tommaso is also involved with the Ethical AI Alliance; he helped create the World AI Harm Map that will be presented at the UN General Assembly in New York. Outside of VOYCE, Tommaso co-founded and led Bocconi Students Jazz and Classical, a thriving music community of over 300 members, well known for its live music events spanning many genres.
members.field_of_studies: Mathematical and Computing Sciences for Artificial Intelligence
members.companies: Quercia Dev, Ethical AI Alliance, Bocconi Students Jazz and Classical
members.interests: Open source AI tech, Machine learning research, Ethical AI policy, Computing data privacy

members.name: Stefano Serra
members.bio: Stefano Serra is an Italian student at Bocconi, who recently finished the Bachelor in International Economics and Management. He has lived across a number of countries, including Luxembourg, Singapore, and the UK before returning to Italy for his university experience. He will soon begin his Master in Politics and Policy Analysis at Bocconi. Stefano's interests lie in regulation and policy formulations in the dynamic technology setting. He is particularly drawn to the EU's role in shaping them correctly to ensure the Union builds a key role in the ever-growing technology sector. Outside of VOYCE, Stefano is passionate about music, being one of the organisers for Bocconi Students Jazz and Classical, one of the only music associations in Bocconi. He also loves to spend his free time cooking for friends and family.
members.field_of_studies: International Economics and Management, Politics and Policy Analysis
members.interests: Dynamic tech regulation, EU tech positioning, Policy analysis framework, Tech sector formulation

members.name: Steffen Timmann
members.bio: Steffen Timmann is a German doctoral student with a Bachelor in Industrial Engineering from KIT and a Master in Management and Technology from TUM. His current research at the HHL Graduate School of Management focuses on Venture Clienting and Venture Capital, with the goal of improving the value of startup technologies in established corporations. Steffen is particularly interested in the strategic, regulatory, and societal dimensions of innovative technologies, particularly sustainable technologies, the future of mobility, energy, and renewables. He is also drawn to industrial tech and emerging disruptive technologies such as artificial intelligence and blockchain. In his personal life, he enjoys doing various sports, with a strong passion for football and calisthenics, and loves diving deep into new and exciting topics.
members.uni: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT), Technical University of Munich (TUM), HHL Graduate School of Management
members.interests: Venture capital clienting, Startup corporate integration, Sustainable technology mobility, AI blockchain framework

members.name: Katarina Malešev
members.bio: Katarina Malešev is a Serbian student at Bocconi, currently enrolled in the Bachelor of Science in Economic and Social Sciences (BESS). Her academic work focuses on economic and financial systems and public policy, including monetary policy, regulatory frameworks, and the role of institutions in shaping market outcomes. In parallel with her studies, she contributes to VOYCE as a writer, where she develops analyses on topics of emerging technologies. Her work engages with EU policy frameworks, including the AI Act and digital governance strategies, where she examines their implications for institutional design. With a strong interest in European technology policy, she regularly explores how the EU approaches the governance of the tech industry, particularly in areas such as artificial intelligence, digital markets and financial innovation. Her broader focus lies in understanding how regulatory frameworks shape technological development and how Europe positions itself in a rapidly evolving global tech landscape.
members.interests: EU AI Act compliance, Digital governance strategy, Financial market innovation, Tech industry positioning

members.name: Sara Farinella
members.bio: Sara Farinella is an Italian BA graduate in International Relations from the University of Milan. During her final year at the University of Geneva, she engaged closely with international political dynamics and the European Union's role in global governance. In her thesis on hybrid warfare, she explored how technological innovation intersects with security and international affairs, focusing on emerging technologies and critical digital infrastructures as both strategic vulnerabilities and new policy frontiers for the EU. At VOYCE, she examines the political challenges posed by technological development and its impact on international politics. When she's not working or studying, Sara loves to chat and is always up to something. She is constantly exploring new hobbies, meeting people, and discovering the world around her.
members.uni: University of Milan, University of Geneva
members.interests: Hybrid warfare dynamics, Digital infrastructure safety, Critical tech vulnerability, Global governance frameworks

members.name: Matteo Mio
members.bio: Matteo Mio is an Italian student, raised between Italy and Switzerland, currently enrolled in a Bachelor's in Economics and Politics at the LSE through Forward College's international program. Passionate about innovation and social progress, he manifests his curiosities through reading, writing and debating, touching on topics such as the startup ecosystem or European technologic industries as well as general public policy and AI regulation. Through his academic journey, he has studied in Lisbon, is currently based in Paris and is projected to finish his bachelor in Berlin. He is also working in Automations and AI integration consulting as part of a freelancing group and loves to discuss such topics with other professionals and interested individuals at events such as Web Summit, which he has attended in the past two editions and hosted a booth at. When he is not studying or working, he can be found at the gym or football field, but also at any random jazz bar in Paris. He also enjoys having politically challenging conversations with friends (or strangers) and traveling to countries of which he does not speak the language.
members.uni: London School of Economics (LSE), Forward College
members.companies: AI Consulting Freelance Group, Web Summit
members.interests: AI regulation consulting, Startup ecosystem tracking, Industrial tech policy, Automation systems integration

members.name: Suriyaa Sundararuban
members.bio: Suriyaa Sundararuban is a German technology professional based in Munich, known for more than a decade of experience in leading Open Source software projects. Suriyaa has worked for IONITY, where he managed over €100 million from Blackrock for EV charging station infrastructure development. At Infineon Technologies, he contributed to the company’s entry into the 5G market and helped navigate the challenges of the US-China trade war. As a Founder’s Associate at Osapiens, he played a key role in alleviating bureaucratic workload for the majority of EU-based companies dealing with supply chain-related sustainability regulations. Within the VOYCE initiative, Suriyaa focuses on developing policies and conducting research to ensure that regulations in the European Union become more business-friendly, embrace Digital Sovereignty and facilitate the quick adoption of new emerging technologies in software and DeepTech. Beyond his work at VOYCE, Suriyaa is passionate about sports, engaging regularly in activities ranging from fitness training to both inline and ice skating.
members.interests: Open source tech leadership, EV charging infrastructure, 5G market entry strategy, DeepTech digital sovereignty
